title: How to Read a Contract in Ten Minutes
excerpt: A quick, structured way to read any agreement so nothing important slips past you.
content:
Most people sign contracts they have only skimmed. A ten-minute read, done in the right order, catches most problems.

## 1. Who and what
Check the names, the dates and exactly what each side is promising. Vague descriptions cause most disputes.

## 2. Money
- the price and when it is due
- late fees and interest
- who pays for extras

## 3. Time and exit
Look for the length of the agreement, automatic renewal and how either side can end it. Note any notice period.

## 4. Risk
Find the clauses on liability, indemnity and confidentiality. If you do not understand one, ask for it in plain words.

## 5. Before you sign
If the amount or the stakes are high, have a lawyer read it. A short consultation costs far less than a dispute.

title: Renting a Home: What to Check First
excerpt: Seven checks to make before you hand over a deposit.
content:
A good tenancy starts before the key is handed over.

## Before you pay
- confirm the person you are paying actually has the right to let the property
- read the agreement in full, including notice periods
- ask what the deposit covers and when it is returned

## On move-in day
Walk through with the landlord and photograph every room, appliance and meter reading. Write down existing damage and have both sides sign the list.

## During the tenancy
Keep payment receipts and send repair requests in writing. A simple paper trail protects you and the landlord.

title: Wills and Estates: A Plain Introduction
excerpt: What a will does, what it cannot do and how to start.
content:
A will is a written statement of who should receive your property and who should look after any children.

## What a will can do
- name your beneficiaries
- appoint an executor
- name a guardian for minor children

## What to gather first
List your property, accounts and debts, and decide who should inherit what. Think about a back-up for each choice.

## Make it valid
Every legal system has formal rules about signing and witnessing. Following them exactly matters more than fancy wording, so use a lawyer or an approved template.

## Review it
Revisit the will after a marriage, birth, move or major change in your finances.

title: Starting a Small Business: The Legal Basics
excerpt: Structure, names, contracts and records for a first-time owner.
content:
Getting the legal basics right early saves money later.

## Choose a structure
A sole trader is simple but personally liable. A company separates your personal assets from the business but needs more paperwork.

## Protect the name
Check that your business name is available and consider registering it as a trademark.

## Put things in writing
Use written terms for customers and clear contracts for suppliers and staff.

## Keep records
Separate business and personal accounts, keep invoices and receipts, and note deadlines for filings and tax. A local accountant or adviser can confirm what applies where you live.
